content.title: Mavericks' birthday dreams give way to harsh reality against Warriors | Dallas Mavericks
content.text: On a day when he and Kyrie Irving each celebrated their birthdays, Jason Kidd talked about what it’s like to have what he called a “born closer” at his disposal, something that should be the case next season when Irving returns to action.Then, after the Mavericks couldn’t close the deal Monday night against the Golden State Warriors, Kidd reiterated that Irving had to go through the same sort of tough times like Cooper Flagg and the rest of the Mavericks are enduring this season.Flagg made a winning play at the end of regulation when he got the Warriors’ defense sucked in and found Naji Marshall all by his lonesome on the three-point line.The shot missed and the Warriors took advantage of the second chance by dominating overtime to beat the Mavericks 137-131 at American Airlines Center.Though it didn’t end successfully, the play was the right one. As was the play with just over a minute left in regulation when Flagg found Max Christie in the corner.Christie’s three-pointer splashed into the net and tied the game at 126. Those points ultimately got the Mavericks to the extra period.The bottom line is that learning to be a “born closer” doesn’t happen right away for any player, no matter how gifted they might be. The Mavericks have had 42 clutch games (within five points in the final five minutes). They have won just 15 of them.“I think it’s going to help everyone,” Kidd said. “Anytime you have real, live plays that come down to the last minute or two minutes, understanding how to get what you want, that’s what the great ones do.“It doesn’t happen overnight. They have to all go through the trials of failure and also success. We’re not looking at it as a fail. Cooper is doing a lot of good. It’s just the ball has not bounced our way. Naji has a wide-open look. Cooper’s making all the right plays, if it’s not for himself it’s for his teammates.”Someday, those plays might involve Flagg electing to take matters into his own hands with game-winning shots. That was an acquired taste for Dirk Nowitzki, among others.But with Irving being out for this season recovering from knee surgery, it has reminded everybody how tough it is to close out tight games successfully.The Mavericks fell to 23-49 and haven't won at AAC since Jan. 22. The Warriors are 34-38 and their win officially meant the Mavericks are eliminated from any postseason contention, although that ship sailed a long time ago, unofficially.(Nicole Malunowicz/Dallas Mavericks)Flagg finished with a monster stat line of 32 points, nine assists, four rebounds and two steals, although he also had seven of the Mavericks' 23 turnovers, which the Warriors turned into 29 points.But the execution down the stretch, regardless of whether shots went in, was impressive.“Every opposing team, especially down the stretch, knows that he’s the guy we want to go to to score, to put us in position to win," said Christie. "And I thought twice tonight he did a great job of making the right play, especially the last shot that Naji had. It was the shot we wanted. Naji’s man helped off him and he was wide-open. And that’s exactly what we wanted. We know Naji can make that and we’re going to take that shot 10 times out of 10.“Us as teammates should be grateful to have someone like that. I think it’s important to make the right play and he does that.”Flagg learning how to finish games is a slow process, but he feels he's already ahead of the curve in that regard.“Got a good switch," Flagg said of the last play of regulation. "I was able to beat him off the dribble and I saw two or three guys from that side collapsing to the rim. I think I could have probably got an OK look."But I look to my left and see Naji with nobody within 10 feet of him. I just made the right basketball play. I made the pass that I thought was best for the scenario. It’s not pre-determined. Just try to read the game at a high level as it’s happening. If I feel two guys collapse, you just try to make the simple play."The outcome put a damper on the good times that started when Kidd and Irving got serenaded at the Mavericks’ morning walk-through by the rookies on the roster and a few hours later, Kidd, who turned 53, could reflect on what a season like this has been like.In short, he has been reminded just how important somebody like Irving is, a reminder that came again against the Warriors.“I told him (Irving) we missed him a lot this year on the floor,” he said.And that moment gave Kidd a chance to dream a little.“When you talk about Kai, at the offensive end, (having him) would help in all categories, shooting, scoring and the biggest (thing) is that if you put us down for 40 clutch games, you have a closer – a born closer,” Kidd said. “I’m not going to say he’s going to win all 40 games for you, but it puts you in a better seat.“And so, having that option will definitely help us if we’re going to talk about next season. For us to not have him all year, that’s impossible to cover up by committee, just because of the things he can do at the highest level. For him to be healthy next year, hopefully that puts us in a better seat.”Indeed, the future with Irving and, hopefully, Dereck Lively II joining Flagg when the 2026-27 season opens is enticing, especially considering Flagg had one of his best games of the season on Monday.It went for naught in overtime when the Warriors scored the first seven points behind Moses Moody, Brandin Podziemski and Gary Payton II.The Mavericks never had a possession to tie or take a lead after that.The Warriors received a scary-looking blow when Moody went down as he tried to leap for a breakaway dunk, but appeared to have his knee give way.After the game, players from both teams were gathered near the X-ray room at AAC to show support for Moody.X: @ESefko
